sources.entry: Gibson - Screen saver that draws a hacker film dashboard from real system telemetry.

summary.one_liner: Gibson is a macOS screen saver that shows a hacker-film security dashboard, mixing real system telemetry (processes, CPU, memory, disk, network) with invented panels for visual effect.
summary.what_it_does: It draws seventeen panels on a grid that scales to any display, including a wireframe globe, radar, live process table, dial clusters, hex dump, oscilloscope, scrolling session log, file vault, and falling digits. Process table, per-core CPU, load average, memory, swap, disk capacity, network throughput, host and macOS details, uptime, and thermal state are read from the host machine. Many other panels, including the user account table, file grid, session log, radar contacts, and globe markers, are synthesized and labeled as fake in the README. Options include four colour schemes (phosphor green, amber CRT, ice cyan, neon magenta), three layouts, and toggles for live metrics, masking host name and addresses, CRT scanlines, and signal glitches. Turning off live metrics stops sampling the host entirely. It is a universal binary with no dependencies beyond system frameworks.
use_cases: display a hacker-style dashboard as a screen saver
show live CPU and memory stats on screen
monitor system processes visually on a secondary display
decorative retro terminal wallpaper for an office
learn SwiftUI or AppKit screen saver development from source
preview panel layouts in a desktop window while developing
how_to_run: Download Gibson.saver.zip from a release, unzip, and double click to install
git clone the repository, then cd Gibson
make demo (runs the panels in a plain window without installing)
notable: Mixes real host telemetry with clearly labeled invented panels
Mask option hides host name, user, and addresses, useful on a lock screen
make demo runs the panels in a resizable window for fast development iteration
Universal binary for Apple silicon and Intel, notarised releases, no dependencies
Each panel throttles its own redraw rate independently
caveats: macOS caches the picker tile and old builds, so the picker may show stale versions (see docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md)
Many panels show fabricated data, including fake account names, passwords and balances
